report.summary: Chunk 2 of daedalus/spine/picker.py: defines constants for regex patterns, source bands, exit codes, and helper functions _slug, _short_hash, _strs, _clamp.
risks: SOURCE_BANDS ordering | medium | The comment states that map_* bands sit above inventory ones, but the actual values show map_island=800, map_shim=700, inventory_island=400, inventory_stale=300. This matches the claim, but the comment also says 'docref' is ranked below unreachable capability and above stale inventory, and its value 500 is between map_shim (700) and inventory_island (400), which is consistent. However, the comment about 'hotspot' being at 100 is not explicitly justified. No risk detected.

_ABBREV_SHA_RE | low | The regex allows up to 64 hex characters, but SHA-256 is 64 chars. The comment says 'anything shorter than 7 is not an identifier', but the regex allows lengths from 7 to 64, which is consistent. No risk.

handoff.purpose: Define constants and helper functions for the picker module.

symbols.name: _SHA_RE
symbols.note: Regex matching a git object name (40 hex digits or 64 for SHA-256).

symbols.name: _ABBREV_SHA_RE
symbols.note: Regex for abbreviated SHA (7 to 64 hex digits).

symbols.name: SOURCE_BANDS
symbols.note: Dictionary mapping source names to priority bands.

symbols.name: SOURCE_ORDER
symbols.note: Tuple of source names in priority order.

symbols.name: EXIT_BY_STATE
symbols.note: Mapping from state string to exit code.

symbols.name: _slug
symbols.note: Convert text to a slug (lowercase, alphanumeric, hyphenated).

symbols.name: _short_hash
symbols.note: Return first n hex digits of SHA-256 hash of text.

symbols.name: _strs
symbols.note: Coerce a value to a tuple of non-empty strings.

symbols.name: _clamp
symbols.note: Clamp a float between lo and hi.

claims.text: The shortest abbreviation a recorded head may use. git's own default floor is 7; anything shorter is not an identifier, it is a coincidence waiting to happen (a 1-char 'prefix' matches ~1 HEAD in 16).
claims.why: The constant _MIN_ABBREV is set to 7, and the regex _ABBREV_SHA_RE uses {7,64}.

claims.text: The two map_* bands sit ABOVE the inventory ones, and that ordering is the whole argument for this source existing.
claims.why: SOURCE_BANDS has map_island=800, map_shim=700, inventory_island=400, inventory_stale=300. The map bands are higher.

claims.text: docs/FEATURE_INVENTORY.json is HAND-WRITTEN and was measured thirty commits stale, while docs/architecture-state.json is GENERATED and covered by a digest and a drift gate.
claims.why: No such files are present in this chunk. The claim refers to external files.

claims.text: When two sources disagree about the same tree, the one that cannot silently rot is the one to work from.
claims.why: This is a design statement not verifiable from the given code.

claims.text: An explicitly curated, revision-bound task outranks inferred work. The queue is an operator decision, not a stronger measurement.
Prose that contradicts the code it describes. Ranked BELOW unreachable capability and ABOVE a stale inventory entry, on importance alone.
claims.why: docref band is 500.0, which is below map_shim (700) and above inventory_stale (300).

claims.text: Deliberately NOT ranked by how convenient it is. As of 2026-07-29 this is the only source whose candidates the installed self-policy actually permits a local writer to touch -- every other source produces surgery under daedalus/ against a write_allow of docs/, tests/, README.md, so the intersection is empty and the loop selects only work it may not do. That makes this source the one that closes the loop, which is a powerful reason to inflate its band and exactly the wrong one: the band states IMPORTANCE, and 'I am allowed to do this' is not a measurement of importance. Smuggling permission into the prior is how a priority order stops meaning what it says.
claims.why: The claim refers to self-policy and write_allow settings not present in this chunk. The band value for docref is 500, but the reasoning about why it is not inflated is not verifiable.

claims.text: The widest a measurement may move a candidate inside its band. Kept strictly smaller than the gap between bands so a measurement can never silently reorder the stated priority -- not even into a TIE that the sort's own tie-break would then have to settle. If a reorder is wanted, the BAND must be edited, which is a visible decision. A test pins this inequality.
claims.why: BAND_SPAN is 50.0. The smallest gap between consecutive bands in SOURCE_BANDS is 100.0 (e.g., between 900 and 800, 800 and 700, etc.). So 50 < 100, the inequality holds. However, the claim about a test is uncheckable.

claims.text: THREE values, not two, because 'a candidate is waiting for you' and 'the runner changed nothing' are different facts and a wrapper that collapses them will eventually report an empty run as a ready patch.
claims.why: There are three exit codes: EXIT_CANDIDATE (0), EXIT_FAILED (1), EXIT_NO_CHANGE (2).

claims.text: A FOURTH value, for the same reason there are three: 'a source could not be consulted' and 'the sources are healthy and there is no work' are different facts, and they were previously indistinguishable to a caller -- both exited 0 on a dry run and both exited 1 under --once.
0 still means, and only ever means, that work is waiting.

Hand-maintained JSON does not have a schema checker standing behind it, so every list-shaped field is read defensively: a string where a list was expected is a typo, not a reason to drop a real work item.
claims.why: The function _strs handles None, str, list, and tuple, treating a bare string as a single-element tuple.

observations.what: The regex _SHA_RE matches 40 or 64 hex digits, covering both SHA-1 and SHA-256.
SOURCE_ORDER omits 'docref' and 'hotspot' compared to SOURCE_BANDS keys.
The comment about 'a test pins this inequality' is uncheckable.
